title: Bina and tevuna: abstract understanding, and the power to apply it
overview:
Chapter 1 taught *hisbonenus* as it rises to *chachma*; chapter 2 brings it down to the emotions and to action. *Bina* has two levels. *Bina* itself is abstract understanding: the *tafsan* with a sharp grasp, the *Gemara* learned *b'iyun* that yields no *halacha*, pure science, an idea that is still a *hiyuli*. *Tevuna*, the light of *bina* spreading out, is applied understanding, and it comes from *kelita*: absorbing the idea until it is the way you think. Then, like the shepherd who draws deep water up to the sheep, the man of *tevuna* can rule in a particular case, explain the depth simply, and feel it in his heart.

*Tevuna* has its own depth, length and width; its letters spell *ben u'vas*, because the emotions are born from *tevuna*, the lower mother, which also gives them their intellect and keeps them going. The way to get it is the double *nun* of *hisbonenus*: go over the idea again and again, in your own words, until it sinks in.

terms.gloss: applied understanding: the light of bina spreading out into application, into the emotions, and into explaining it to others
absorption: the idea sinks in until it becomes the way you think, the root of tevuna
a man of tevuna, who draws the deep waters up so that anyone can drink
a grasper: a quick, sharp mind whose understanding stays in the theory
raw potential: an idea of which nobody yet knows what will come out
grasping a concept while it stays outside of you, as opposed to kelita
son and daughter, the letters of tevuna: love and fear, born from tevuna
the lower mother: tevuna, the womb that actually gives birth to the middos
the upper mother: bina, the real source of the middos but not their direct source
"and so": the conclusion that applies the idea to me, which turns understanding into emotion
thought itself, the letters of thought, coming from Malchus of tevuna
the straight, long nun: the length; the second nun of hisbonenus, which carries bina into tevuna

sections.title: Tevuna is bina spreading out: the man of tevuna draws up the deep waters
sections.summary: *Bina* has two levels, *bina* and *tevuna*. *Bina* is abstract understanding; *tevuna* is applied understanding, the light of *bina* spreading out, and it comes when the idea is absorbed so well that it becomes yours. Then, like the shepherd who draws deep water up to the sheep, a man of *tevuna* can bring the depth out so simply that it is as if it was never deep.

phrases.he: (ב) והנה ידוע שיש בבינה עצמה ב' מדרגות, בינה ותבונה,
phrases.en: It's known that *bina* itself has two levels: *bina* and *tevuna*.

phrases.he: וענין התבונה הוא בחינת התפשטות אור הבינה
phrases.en: The idea of *tevuna* is the spreading out of the light of *bina*.
Like it says in the *Zohar*,

phrases.he: דאבא ואמא תתאין הם ישראל סבא ותבונה,
phrases.en: the lower father and mother, meaning the lower *chachma* and *bina*, are called *Yisroel Saba*, grandfather Israel, and *tevuna*.

blocks.text: Chapter 1 explained *hisbonenus* (contemplation): *iyun* (close analysis), *omek hadaas* (the depth of *daas*), the *ma'amik* (one who delves), the *Chabad* of *Chabad*. Now we see how it brings you not only up to *chachma* and *Keser* (crown) but down to the *middos* (emotional attributes) of the *sechel* (intellect), and on to actual emotions and *maaseh* (action).

**It's known that bina itself has two levels: bina and tevuna.** *Tanya* mentions *tevuna*, but few know what it is. *Bina* (understanding), explained in the last chapter, sees every part and detail of a thing; *tevuna* is applied understanding, as against abstract.

**The idea of tevuna is the spreading out of the light of bina.** The *Zohar* calls **the lower chachma and bina** *Yisroel Saba* **and tevuna**: the *hispashtus* (spreading forth) of each. What makes it spread?

phrases.he: מצד קליטתה היטב בכלי המקבל ההשגה דבינה,
phrases.en: This is because the idea is very well received, or very well absorbed, into the vessel that receives the understanding of *bina*.

phrases.he: על כן מתפשט בה להביאה בכמה ענינים נבדלים מעצם ההשגה,
phrases.en: Therefore, the idea spreads out in it to come into many, many different things that are separate from the abstract understanding.
And this is what is called a man of *tevuna*.

phrases.he: כמו מים עמוקים כו' איש תבונה ידלנה.
phrases.en: Like it says in the verse, deep waters... a man of *tevuna* can draw it out.

blocks.text: Because **the idea is very well received** into **the vessel** of *bina*, it **spreads out** into **many, many different things that are separate from the abstract understanding.** When an idea really sinks in and becomes one with you, it is yours, and you can apply it outside the textbook. Of the deep waters, **a man of tevuna can draw it out.**

phrases.en: the deep waters,
that is the depth of *bina*,
The depth of *bina* remains hidden in yourself.
and a man of *tevuna*,
only such a person that has this type of understanding
can draw it out,
and can draw it from its hiddenness,
to bring it out into application
many different ways,
to quench the thirst of the *mekablim*.

phrases.he: כמו הדולה מים עמוקים להשקות הצאן כו'
phrases.en: like somebody that draws deep waters to water sheep.
and this is like what we see,
tangibly,

phrases.he: שבהיות השכל והסברא עמוקים ביותר מהכיל בהשגת אדם,
phrases.en: that when an idea or a *sevara* is very deep, and it's too deep for a person to grasp,

phrases.he: הנקרא מים עמוקים כו', שהוא בחינת עומק המושג הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: that's the depth of understanding that we discussed in the last *perek*,
which the length and the width of the idea come out from that point.

blocks.text: **The deep waters** are **the depth of bina**, hidden within, like the *omek hamusag* (the depth of the concept), explained only through its length and width. **Only such a person** as has *tevuna* **can draw it out** of **its hiddenness** in **many different ways, to quench the thirst of the mekablim** (the receivers).

blocks.title: The shepherd at the deep well
blocks.text: The sheep are thirsty, and the water in the well is very deep. The shepherd lowers a bucket and brings it up: the same water, no longer deep. *Yidlena* is drawing it with the bucket; *yishavena*, pouring it into a trough.

**And this is like what we see**: an idea **too deep for a person to grasp** is called deep waters, **the depth of understanding that we discussed in the last perek**, the source of its length and width.

phrases.en: And specifically a person that has this power of *tevuna* can draw out this depth.

phrases.he: פירוש שיוציא לאור בחינת העלם העומק המושג
phrases.en: He's able to bring out to light, in order to reveal, this hidden depth of the idea,
until a person's mind can grasp it, can understand it,
as if it wasn't deep at all.

phrases.he: כמו הדולה מים עמוקים שמקרב את העומק כו'
phrases.en: Like the shepherd that draws the water from the well, that now brings it close to the sheep, as if it wasn't deep at all.
And based on this,
we must say

phrases.he: שכח התבונה הוא כח המתפשט מכח הבינה להביא עומקה לגילוי למטה למקבלים כו'
phrases.en: that the power of *tevuna* is the ability to bring out the understanding of *bina*, to bring its depth so that it should be understood to other people, to the *mekabel*.

blocks.text: **A person that has this power of tevuna can draw out this depth** **until a person's mind can grasp it**, **as if it wasn't deep at all**: the shepherd brings the water up and sets it right in front of the sheep.
So **the power of tevuna is the ability to bring out the understanding of bina** to others: making an idea simpler for someone who cannot grasp it alone comes from *tevuna*.

sections.title: The tafsan: a sharp grasp that stays in the theory
sections.summary: Someone who is not a man of *tevuna* can still have a quick, sharp grasp, a *tafsan*, and yet his understanding stays in his own *bina*: he cannot teach it or apply it. Even its length and width are only the textbook's examples, all within the theory, and its depth stays hidden even to him.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כשאינו איש תבונות,
phrases.en: On the other hand, when somebody is not a man of *tevunos*,

phrases.he: גם שהוא בעל השגה במוח דבינה
phrases.en: even if he does understand personally, he's able to understand the idea with his faculty of *bina*,
which the world calls a *tafsan*,

phrases.he: יוכל להיות שהשגתו נשארת רק כמו שהיא בעצם, במוח הבינה שלו
phrases.en: it can be that his understanding will remain the way it is, just in his faculty of *bina*,
that's called just his spirit of understanding,

phrases.he: ולא יבוא ממנה שום התפשטות למטה
phrases.en: and no application will come out from it,

phrases.he: בענין נבדל שחוץ מן עצם ההשגה כלל
phrases.en: in any matter that's separate from the abstract understanding at all.

blocks.text: **When somebody is not a man of tevunos**, he does not absorb the idea so as to bring it out simply. He may be what **the world calls a tafsan** (a grasper), quick and sharp, and still be unable to teach it.

**His understanding will remain the way it is, just in his faculty of bina**: abstract theory he cannot explain or apply, **just his spirit of understanding**, **and no application will come out from it**.

phrases.he: וגם שיש בהשגה אורך ורוחב ועומק כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: and even though the understanding of the theory itself has a length and a width and a depth,
even all of this, even the length and the width, are just part of the abstract understanding,
as it is, in its natural state.

phrases.he: אבל לא שיתגלה למטה בענין נבדל,
phrases.en: But it doesn't mean that it will be expressed in something separate,

phrases.he: ומכל שכן עומק המושג הרי נשאר בעומקו בהעלם לעצמו,
phrases.en: and for sure the depth of his understanding remains hidden to himself,
and even the length and the width
are all within the idea itself,
the way it is in its place alone.

blocks.text: **The length and the width** too **are just part of the abstract understanding**: the textbook needs *meshalim* (analogies) and examples to explain the idea, but all within the theory.
**It doesn't mean that it will be expressed in something separate.** The depth stays **hidden to himself**, so he cannot explain it, and the length and width are all theory.

sections.title: The example: a Talmudic pilpul that yields no ruling, an idea that is only hiyuli
sections.summary: Someone can learn a *Gemara* in depth, with all the *sevaros* of the commentators, and still not know the *halacha*: the reasoning stays an abstract thing that rules neither liable nor exempt. Such an idea is a *hiyuli*, of which nobody yet knows what will come out.

phrases.en: And an example for all of this:

phrases.he: הנה אנו רואים בעומק הפלפול בתלמוד וטעמים בסברות רבות כך וכך
phrases.en: when a person's learning *Gemara*, and they learn a whole *pilpul* with many different reasons and *sevaros*, one this way and one that way,
even when they understand it very well,

phrases.he: אבל לא יוכלו עדיין להוציא לאור מעצם השכל איזה פסק דין חייב או זכאי כלל

blocks.text: **When a person's learning Gemara**, **a whole pilpul with many different reasons and sevaros**, with all the *Rishonim* and *Acharonim* (earlier and later commentators), **even when they understand it very well**, they cannot draw any ruling out of it, liable or exempt.

One can learn *Gemara* (the Talmud) *b'iyun* (in depth), understand its *sevaros* (lines of reasoning) very well, and, as usually happens, not know the *halacha* (the law in practice) from it. They are almost opposite ways of learning: *b'iyun* goes up, away from the practical; *halacha* goes down. Unless you learn *l'halacha* on purpose, you must reverse your thinking to see it.
That is why starting *semicha* (rabbinic ordination) is a big change in many people's way of learning: used to *Gemara b'iyun* without *halacha*, they are suddenly learning it *l'halacha*.

phrases.en: This means

phrases.he: שלא יוכל להוציא מתוך הסברה איזה חיוב על פי זה השכל ולא איזה זכות על פי זה השכל

blocks.text: **This means** he cannot bring any liability or merit out of the reasoning. He knows the *sevara* according to *Rashi*, *Tosfos*, the *Rosh*, the *Ran*, the *Rif*, the *Rambam* and the *Ramban*; ask him how it comes out in a given case, and he does not know yet. That is a whole other level of understanding.

phrases.he: כי עדיין אין השכל והסברה רק השכלה שכליות לבד,
phrases.en: Because right now, it's just an abstract, intellectual thing.

phrases.he: בלתי ימצא ממנו שום התפשטות בהטיות לענין נבדל הימנה,
שהוא לחייב על ידה או לזכות על ידה
phrases.en: which means to find guilt because of it or merit because of it.

blocks.text: **Right now, it's just an abstract, intellectual thing**, leaning to nothing separate: a *pilpul* on what defines the liability. Is it on the *gavra* (the person) or the *cheftza* (the object), because of this or because of that?

blocks.title: The first inquiry in Bava Kama
blocks.text: Learning *Bava Kama*, Rabbi Walters met a whole *chakira* (inquiry): are you liable for your property's damage through *he'eder hashmira* (the failure to guard it), or through a real obligation tied to your money? You see no *nafka mina* (practical difference). Ask for one, and you are told: if a man betroths a woman on condition that this is the reason for the law.
For now they want the thing itself; the practical can come later. So it does not lean **to find guilt because of it or merit because of it.**

phrases.en: This is like something that is a *hiyuli*, like an essence,

phrases.he: שלא נודע עדיין מה ימצא ממנה ומה יעשה בה
phrases.en: that we do not yet know what will come out from it or what can be done with it.
In Yiddish we would say: the idea itself as it is, meaning the abstract theory,

phrases.he: ער קאן מיט אים נישט טאן קיין זאך ניט
phrases.en: he can't do anything with it,

phrases.he: צו קערין לזכות או לחוב כו')
phrases.en: to lean the judgment to merit or to liability.

blocks.text: **This is like something that is a hiyuli**, raw potential, as chapters 10 and 11 explained: **we do not yet know what will come out from it**, since it could come out in so many ways. In Yiddish we would say: **the idea itself as it is**; **he can't do anything with it, to lean the judgment to merit or to liability.**

sections.title: The power of tevuna: application to a ruling, to the heart and to thought
sections.summary: *Tevuna* brings the abstract understanding down into what is separate from it: a ruling of guilty or innocent, an emotion in the heart, many ways of thinking it. *Bina* is pure science and *Gemara b'iyun*; *tevuna* is applied science, *halacha*, and knowing how to set up a kosher kitchen.

phrases.en: However,
the power of *tevuna* that spreads out from the faculty of *bina*:

phrases.he: היינו מה שביכולתו להביא עצם ההשגה לבחינת התפשטות למטה ממנה
phrases.en: it's in the ability of this power to bring the abstract understanding to application in something lower than it,
in anything separate from it,
whether that means to find the judgment of guilt or innocence,
or to bring it to an excitement in your heart, that you should have an emotional reaction because of this understanding,

phrases.he: וכן להביאה במחשבה בכמה אופנים שונים כו'.
phrases.en: and also to be able to bring it into thought in many different ways, that you should be able to explain the idea to yourself in all different ways, conceptualize it, even the depth of it, in many ways.

blocks.text: **However**, being stuck in theory belongs only to *bina* itself. **The power of tevuna that spreads out from the faculty of bina** can **bring the abstract understanding to application in something lower than it**: **to find the judgment of guilt or innocence**, **or to bring it to an excitement in your heart**, **and also to be able to bring it into thought in many different ways**, even its depth.
So this is the general difference: *bina* is the abstract understanding, still like a *hiyuli* to its applications; *tevuna* is the power of applied understanding.

It is the difference between *Gemara* as *pilpul* and *halacha*. Rabbi Walters thinks *Chabad* used to stress *Gemara l'halacha*; he is not sure why that changed, or whether the *pilpul* style just became popular. He heard it was always done that way; it might say so in *Kuntres Etz HaChaim*.

blocks.title: Pure and applied science
blocks.text: It is like pure and applied science. Pure mathematics is the theory, numbers and formulas applied to nothing yet. Applied mathematics is engineering: working out the trajectories to send something to the moon, or, for a bridge, all the variables, the pressure, the wind, what an earthquake would do to the structure.

blocks.title: Learning shechita in the Gemara and in the Shulchan Aruch
blocks.text: Learning *Shulchan Aruch* (the Code of Jewish Law) is practical understanding: not the doing, but an idea tied to it. The *Gemara* on *shechita* (ritual slaughter) asks why this *shechita* is kosher and that one not, seeking the one factor everything rests on: that search for the depth is *bina*. Learning what to do is *tevuna*.

blocks.title: The hard steel knife
blocks.text: Much of *tevuna* is circumstantial. The main thing in *shechita* is that the knife cuts by its sharpness, not by ripping or by your pressure. So in practice you want a very sharp knife of very hard steel that will not nick, since a nick rips. But really you may *shecht* with anything sharp, and not even that sharp: you could go back and forth all day and it would be kosher, as long as you are not pressing and it is not ripping. The hard steel knife is a practical matter.

sensitivity.reason: A ruling on shechita stated loosely under his name: that a slow cut going back and forth all day is kosher.
sensitivity.publishable: Much of *tevuna* is circumstantial. The main thing in *shechita* is that the knife cuts by its sharpness, not by ripping or by your pressure. So in practice you want a very sharp knife of very hard steel that will not nick, since a nick rips. The hard steel knife is a practical matter.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: Whether "not even that sharp ... all day" misstates the law (a pause in the cut, shehiya, disqualifies) or is a fair illustration of what the law requires; the publishable text drops only that clause.

blocks.title: Setting up a kosher kitchen
blocks.text: You see this difference, between the abstract idea and a practical way to do it, in how *bochurim* (yeshiva boys) and girls learn, say, *kashrus* (the kosher laws). Even *bochurim* learning *semicha* learn much more of the theory. But setting up a kitchen so that it stays kosher in practice, with separate dishes and separate burners, arranged to cut down the problems, "is a whole nother *chachma*": a different power of understanding altogether.

sensitivity.reason: Contrasts the way yeshiva boys and girls learn kashrus as a generalisation about men and women.

sections.title: The middos within bina stay in theory; the man of tevuna brings the ruling out
sections.summary: *Bina* has emotions of its own, the intellect that leans to merit or to guilt, so it seems that *tevuna* is not needed. But those emotions stay hidden in the theory; only the man of *tevuna*, who has not just grasped the idea (*tefisa*) but absorbed it (*kelita*), can rule in a particular case and explain the depth to anyone.

phrases.en: However, seemingly we see
that seemingly *bina* itself has *middos*,
which are called the seven lower *sefiros* of *bina*.
And these are called the emotions of the intellect,

phrases.he: המטה כלפי זכות או שכל מטה כלפי חוב
phrases.en: an intellect that leans towards merit or an intellect that leans towards guilt.

blocks.text: **Seemingly bina itself has middos, which are called the seven lower sefiros of bina**: then why do we need *tevuna*? **These are called the emotions of the intellect**: the intellect tells you *chayav* (liable) or *patur* (exempt).

phrases.he: היינו כמו שהמדות שבשכל הן בעצם ההשגה עדיין בהעלם
phrases.en: So the emotions of *bina* itself are the emotions of the intellect the way they are in the abstract theory, and they're still hidden.

phrases.he: אבל להביא בחינת התגלותן בדבר נבדל,
phrases.en: But to be able to reveal them in something separate,

phrases.he: כמו להורות בענין מקרה דבר מה על פי השכל והסברא הזאת,
phrases.en: to say the ruling in a particular case based on this intellect and this logic,

phrases.he: להטות את המשפט של זה הענין לחסד וגבורה שבו דוקא,
phrases.en: to influence the judgment of this case to either the *chesed* or *gevura*,

phrases.he: הרי איש תבונה דווקא יוציא לאור מן המדות שבבינה כו'
phrases.en: specifically a person of *tevuna* is able to bring out the ruling from the emotions of *bina*.

blocks.text: **The emotions of bina itself are the emotions of the intellect the way they are in the abstract theory, and they're still hidden.** **To say the ruling in a particular case based on this intellect and this logic**, inclining it to *chesed* or *gevura* (kindness or severity), takes **a person of tevuna**.

In the *Gemara*'s *pilpul* it is hidden that one says *chayav* and another *patur*; even a ruling there is an abstract case. As with *Gemara* against *semicha*, most people are far from seeing the ruling. Seeing how the theory applies to a particular case belongs to an *ish tevuna* (a man of *tevuna*).

phrases.he: ואיש תבונות היינו כח הקולט בכי טוב לעצם ההשגה,
phrases.en: A man of *tevunos* means the ability to really absorb the theory, to really internalize it, to really become one with the way you think and feel and view the world.

phrases.he: על כן מתפשטת ההשגה בו לעשות ולהורות בה כמה ענינים נבדלים לגמרי
phrases.en: Therefore, since this idea becomes one with him, it's able to spread out: he's able to use it, to make a judgment based on it, in many things that are totally separate from the theory.

phrases.he: וגם ביכולתו להביא את עומק בינה לידי גילוי כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: And he can also bring out the depth of *bina* and explain it in a way that's understandable, like we said before.

blocks.text: **A man of tevunos** can **really absorb the theory**, until it is one with how he thinks and sees the world. So it is **able to spread out**: he can **make a judgment based on it** **in many things that are totally separate from the theory**, and explain its depth understandably.

The depth of *bina* is just *tefisa* (grasping): you hold the concept, but apart from you, something you appreciate, not how you think. *Tevuna* needs *kelita* (absorption): the idea sinks in until you think that way. Then you see it in every case, give examples and *meshalim* from daily life that make the depth of *bina* clear to an ordinary person, and apply it.

sections.title: Yisroel Saba and tevuna, Malchus of tevuna and the letters of thought
sections.summary: *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna* are the emotions of *chachma* and of *bina* as they come out into application: the intuitive feel, and the power to explain. *Malchus* of *tevuna* attaches the concept to words, the letters of thought, an outer vessel for analysis; and from it comes thought itself, *Leah*.

phrases.he: (והיינו בחינת אבא ואמא תתאין ישראל סבא ותבונה
phrases.en: And this is the idea that the lower father and mother are *Yisroel Saba* and *tevuna*.

phrases.he: ישראל סבא מדות דחכמה ותבונה מדות דבינה
phrases.en: *Yisroel Saba* is the *middos*, the emotions, of *chachma*, and *tevuna* is the emotions of *bina*.
But these are the emotions of *chachma* and *bina* the way they come outside, to be revealed outside of the *etzem* idea.
And what's the idea of *Malchus* of *tevuna*?
This is the intellect that comes into thought.
This is called the letters of intellectual thought,
which the intellect is enclothed in this type of thought.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת כלי חיצוני למחשבה עיונית
phrases.en: This is the external vessel for analytical thought.

phrases.he: שהוא גלוי השגה דבינה עצמה מצד עצם השכל והסברא כו'
phrases.en: Which this intellectual thought is revealing the actual understanding of *bina* itself, relating to the intellect and the logic.

phrases.he: ומבחינת מלכות דתבונה נמשך שרש אותיות המחשבה עצמה שנקרא לאה כו'

phrases.en: And this is the large *dalet* of the word *Echad*.

blocks.text: **And this is the idea that the lower father and mother** **are Yisroel Saba and tevuna**: **Yisroel Saba is the middos, the emotions** of *chachma*, **and tevuna is the emotions of bina.** *Yisroel Saba* is application by intuition.

blocks.title: Shatik Rav: the ruling he could not explain
blocks.text: Someone with a gut feeling that a thing is right or wrong, who cannot say why, is like *Yisroel Saba*. So *shatik Rav* (Rav was silent) in *Beitza*. The *machlokes*, he thinks, is over an egg laid on *Yom Tov*, *muktza* as *nolad* (newly come into being), against a cow born on *Yom Tov*, which is not. Rav ruled that they differ; asked why, he could not answer, but he did not retract. He saw the difference by intuition: that is *Yisroel Saba*. Then someone else explained it: that is *tevuna*.

**But these are the emotions of chachma and bina the way they come outside, to be revealed outside of the etzem idea** (the idea itself): not the *middos* contained in the theory, but the theory brought out into application.

**And what's the idea of Malchus of tevuna?** *Malchus* (kingship) of *tevuna* applies the idea to thought, speech and action: **the letters of intellectual thought** that clothe the intellect. It ties the theory to words, so that you think of the idea in those words.

blocks.title: The child's rubber stamps
blocks.text: A child's rubber stamp has a cow on one side and the word on the other, and stamps C-O-W: the thing and the word. *Malchus* of *tevuna* connects the concept to the words.

**This is the external vessel for analytical thought.** Talking to yourself helps the mind work an idea over, but the mind does it without words too: the words are only a *kli* (vessel) that focuses it, not the thought of *bina* itself.

blocks.title: Staring at the tiles
blocks.text: Stare at tiles in a very simple pattern, plain squares or black and white checkers, and your mind keeps making patterns of them: diagonals, lines, boxes. The pattern is too simple, so your *bina* keeps looking for more complicated ones, cutting it up this way and that. Putting it into words for yourself is only a *kli* that helps it along.

**Which this intellectual thought is revealing the actual understanding of bina itself, relating to the intellect and the logic.** So *Malchus* of *tevuna* brings the understanding of *bina* out into thought: another thing *tevuna* does.

From *Malchus* of *tevuna* comes the root of the letters of thought: once ideas are tied to words, you can have the words alone, thought itself, called *Leah* and explained later. **And this is the large dalet of the word Echad.**

sections.title: Ben u'vas: tevuna's three dimensions, and the lower mother who gives birth to the emotions
sections.summary: *Tevuna* has its own depth, length and width: its depth is *kelita*, absorbing the idea; its length is bringing it down into something else, a ruling, an invention, a skill; its width is thinking it in many ways. Its letters spell *ben u'vas*, son and daughter, because the emotions are actually born from *tevuna*, the lower mother, and not from *bina*, the upper mother.

phrases.en: And this is what is called *tevuna*,
which *tevuna* has the letters of *ben u'vas*,

phrases.he: להיות כי גם בתבונה יש ג' דברים,
phrases.en: because *tevuna* also has three things:
a depth, a length, and a width.

blocks.text: **Tevuna has the letters of ben u'vas** (son and daughter), with an extra *hei*, **because tevuna also has three things: a depth, a length, and a width**, like *chachma*, *bina* and *daas* in chapter 1. *Ben u'vas* means it is a source of the *middos*, explained shortly.

phrases.he: העומק הוא עצם כח התבונה הזאת שבאותה ההשגה,
phrases.en: The depth of *tevuna* is the essence of the power of *tevuna* in this understanding,

phrases.he: כמו שהיא בשעה שקולטת אותה כו'
phrases.en: the way that it is at the time that you absorb it.

phrases.he: ובה יוכל עומק ההשגה הנזכר לעיל לבוא לגלוי,
phrases.en: And when a person has this, that they really absorb the idea, then they're able to bring the depth out to reveal it,

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בפסוק איש תבונה ידלנה כו'
phrases.en: like we explained before about how a man of *tevuna* can draw out the deep waters.

blocks.text: **The depth of tevuna is the essence of the power of tevuna**, the understanding that lets you apply, as it is at **the time that you absorb it**. Its main thing is *kelita*: *hasaga* (comprehension) holds the idea outside you; *tevuna* absorbs it.

blocks.title: The Rav who goes over the Shulchan Aruch
blocks.text: It must be how you think and see things. A *Rav* who wants to *paskin* (rule on) *halacha* cannot just learn and understand a *halacha*: he goes over, say, the Alter Rebbe's *Shulchan Aruch* again and again, until he thinks in its logic, order and categories. Seeing through the eyes of the *halacha*, beyond the textbook, he can *paskin* in new situations. So with anything you truly absorb: you can apply it.

**Then they're able to bring the depth out to reveal it**, so that it seems simple: **a man of tevuna** *davka* **can draw out the deep waters**. So the depth of *tevuna* is this *kelita*, taking the idea into your way of thinking.

phrases.en: the length of *tevuna*
is to bring the idea down into something else, a different subject, a different idea,
which is separate from the original idea that you're studying,

phrases.he: להורות בו ולעשות מעשים רבים על ידה כו'
phrases.en: to give advice based on it, or to *paskin* based on it, and to do many different things with it.

blocks.text: **The length of tevuna is to bring the idea down into something else**, **separate from the original idea that you're studying**: **to give advice based on it, or to paskin based on it**, to apply it in your life, or to make money from a theory.

blocks.title: The Greek steam engine and the American steamboat
blocks.text: The ancient Greeks invented a kind of steam engine, applied only much later, in America, as a steamboat. Partly it was technical limits, but also a mindset: the Greeks learned pure science, to understand; America at one time pushed hard to invent and develop technology, more *tevuna* thinking.

blocks.title: From relativity to the bomb
blocks.text: So too with the path from the theory of relativity to the atomic bomb. Einstein's theory was very nice, but only a theory, and some physicists were happy that it explained things. Then he realized that a bomb could be made from it. They told the president that he had better make this bomb before the Russians made it, and so the Manhattan Project began. That is the length of *tevuna*: once you absorb an idea, you can apply it.

sensitivity.reason: A historical slip printed under his name: the warning to the president was about Germany, not the Russians.
sensitivity.publishable: So too with the path from the theory of relativity to the atomic bomb. Einstein's theory was very nice, but only a theory, and some physicists were happy that it explained things. Then he realized that a bomb could be made from it. They told the president that he had better make this bomb, and so the Manhattan Project began. That is the length of *tevuna*: once you absorb an idea, you can apply it.

blocks.text: This matters most to anyone learning a skill, a doctor, a lawyer, a mechanic: he must absorb the lessons to use them or give advice. So with a *Rav*, and with *Chassidus* (Chassidic teaching): to apply it, the main thing is *tevuna*, as the next chapter explains.

phrases.en: And the width:

phrases.he: הוא בחינת התפשטות התבונה בעצם ההשגה,
phrases.en: the width of *tevuna* is to expand, to spread out the idea within the idea itself, to apply the theory within the understanding,

phrases.he: להרחיבה במחשבה בכמה רבוי אופנים שונים
phrases.en: that you should be able to think about the idea in many different ways,
and not just the way it is alone.

blocks.text: **The width of tevuna is to expand, to spread out the idea within the idea itself**, **to think about the idea in many different ways**. You are not bound to the terms you first learned it in: you find examples, explanations and stories to think about it and explain it.

phrases.en: And this, that *tevuna* includes within it *ben* and *bas*,

phrases.he: היינו מה שמתבונה דוקא יולדו המדות בגלוי מהות בפני עצמם,
phrases.en: this represents that specifically from *tevuna* the *middos* are revealed, that they come out to be their own: the source of having an actual emotion, of actual love and actual fear, separate from your intellect, is from *tevuna*.

phrases.he: כי מבינה עצמה לא היו תולדות המדות
phrases.en: Because from *bina* itself the emotions would not be born, they would not come out,

phrases.he: אף על פי שנקרא אם הבנים כו'
phrases.en: even though *bina* is called the mother of the children, which means that it is the source of the emotions,
but it's the upper mother.

blocks.text: **That tevuna includes within it ben and bas** means that **from tevuna the middos are revealed**: actual love and fear, separate from the intellect. The mind still rules, *moach shalit al halev* (the mind rules the heart), but you actually feel the emotion, unlike the *middos* of *bina*, which stay in the theory.

blocks.title: Whoever takes from his fellow
blocks.text: A *sevara* in the *Gemara* holds this man responsible, but how does it apply here? You know *hamotzi mechaveiro alav hara'aya* (whoever takes from his fellow must bring the proof), but are not sure who is taking from whom, so you cannot *paskin*. The emotion is hidden in the theory until you know how to apply it.

**From bina itself the emotions would not be born**: it **is called the mother of the children**, their source, **but it's the upper mother**, *Ima ila'a*, not the direct source. To be moved you must see how it applies to you: you need the *uvchein* ("and so": the conclusion).

phrases.he: מה שאין כן התבונה נקרא אימא תתאה
phrases.en: But *tevuna* is called the lower mother,
to give birth to the *middos*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת ב''ן וב''ת, אהבה ויראה,
phrases.en: And this is the idea of *ben u'vas*, love and fear,
that they are included in *tevuna* specifically,

phrases.he: שהיא בחינת התפשטות אור הבינה למטה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: which *tevuna* is the spreading of the light of *bina* below, to everything separate from *bina*.

blocks.text: **But tevuna is called the lower mother**, *Ima tata'a*, the *uvchein*, **to give birth to the middos.**

blocks.title: The upper mother and the womb
blocks.text: There is really one mother, and *bina* and *tevuna* are two parts of her. Speaking of someone's mother, you mainly mean her mind, feelings and personality, her head and heart: the upper mother. But a child is born from the womb, the lower mother. So *bina*, the real source, is called the mother of the children, but they are born only from *tevuna*. *Tevuna* gets little focus of its own because *hisbonenus*, not yet discussed, is what brings you to it.

**And this is the idea of ben u'vas, love and fear, that they are included in tevuna**, **the spreading of the light of bina below**: it applies the *sechel* to say whether a situation calls for *chesed* or *gevura*.

blocks.title: The lion in the classroom
blocks.text: A child in school learns about Shimshon and the lion: the big teeth, the strength, what a miracle it was to kill one. If he thinks about it he has *tevuna*: lions are dangerous, and so, the *uvchein*, he should fear them. But he feels no fear, because there is no lion in the room: he has no *daas* for it, and it does not touch him. When the lion walks in, his *daas* joins his *tevuna* to the actual emotion.

Even before *daas*, the real emotion is the *tevuna*: the mind saying this is dangerous, get away if it comes near. That is the *moach* (mind) ruling the *lev* (heart). The heart is stirred only when it matters now, but the *midda* comes from there.

sections.title: The intellect of the emotions comes from tevuna, which keeps them going
sections.summary: The *mochin* of the *middos*, the intellect that tells an emotion how to go and keeps it going, come from *tevuna*: G-d maintains the heavens, fire and water, with *tevuna*. *Tevuna* is the intermediary that turns the *middos* of *bina*, which have nothing to do with a particular case, into what I should feel now.

phrases.he: וגם לזה הטעם בחינת המוחין שבמדות נמשך מבחינת התבונה
phrases.en: And this is also the reason why the intellect of the emotions comes from *tevuna*,
as it says, G-d founded the earth with *chachma*,
because the father founds the daughter.

blocks.text: **And this is also the reason why the intellect of the emotions comes from tevuna.** Once there is an emotion, its intellect directs it: *tevuna* brings the *sechel* down and tells the emotion, in each situation, whether to be happy or sad, to like or to hate. That is what keeps the emotion going.

blocks.title: The child who falls down
blocks.text: A small child falls down. At first he is stunned, taking in what happened; then he calms a little, it sinks in, and he cries. Not at once, because his *chachma* and *bina* were busy working it out, and while he was in his mind he felt nothing. Once he realizes that it hurt, he cries.

blocks.title: "Hey, he hit me!"
blocks.text: Someone who is hit is sometimes too stunned to be angry. Once he realizes he was hit and his *sechel* tells him not to let it pass, he grows angry. So with every emotion.
**As it says, G-d founded the earth with chachma, because the father founds the daughter**: *chachma* is the source of *Malchus*, and the earth stands for *Malchus*, as will be explained.

phrases.en: He maintains the heavens with *tevuna*.

phrases.he: שמים הן בחינת המדות, אש מים כידוע
phrases.en: And the heavens represent the two emotions, *esh u'mayim*.

blocks.text: **He maintains the heavens with tevuna.** *Shamayim* (heavens) contracts *esh u'mayim* (fire and water), *chesed* and *gevura*. *Tevuna* maintains them: without the *sechel* telling them what to feel, the feelings fade.

phrases.en: And similarly it says, with *tevuna* they are established,

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת קיום המדות בבחינת המוחין דתבונה שבהם,
phrases.en: which this is the maintenance of the emotions from the *mochin* of *tevuna*.
Because *tevuna* is like a sort of intermediary:

phrases.he: להביא מוחין מבחינת מדות דבינה במדות שבלב
phrases.en: it brings an intellect from the emotions of *bina* to the emotions of the heart.

phrases.he: שזהו כמו כח ההבאה בענין הנבדל, שהוא עיקר ענין התבונה כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: That is like the power of bringing something out into something separate from the *sechel*, and this is the general thing of *tevuna*, like we've been explaining.

blocks.text: **And similarly it says, with tevuna they are established, which this is the maintenance of the emotions from the mochin of tevuna**: the intellect telling the emotions what to feel is what keeps them going.

blocks.title: The tape recorder in the head
blocks.text: A person with an emotion has a little tape recorder going in his head, repeating the same thing. Angry, he keeps telling himself what that man did and that he will not let him get away with it: an *uvchein*. In love, he keeps telling himself how great it is. That keeps the emotion going, and people who want to hype themselves up tell each other the same.

**Tevuna is like a sort of intermediary**: **it brings an intellect from the emotions of bina to the emotions of the heart.** To go from the theoretical *middos* of *bina*, about no particular case, to what I should feel now, *tevuna* turns the *sechel* into an *uvchein*.

blocks.title: The chicken brought to the rabbi
blocks.text: The woman brings her chicken to the rabbi, and he launches into a *pilpul*: the *Rema*, the *Shach*, the *Bach*, this opinion and that. At the end she asks, "So is it kosher or not?" Understanding the theory is not enough; you must carry it to the deed. That is *tevuna*.

Emotions are separate from the *sechel*, so moving something from intellect to emotion **is like the power of bringing something out into something separate from the sechel**, **the general thing of tevuna**. The *middos* of *bina* stay in the theory; *tevuna* applies it outside. Next: how one gets *tevuna*.

sections.title: The two nuns: hisbonenus, bina sheb'bina, brings bina out into tevuna
sections.summary: *Bina* has a bent *nun*, its width, and a straight *nun*, its length, and the name *nun* is spelled with both: the length is included in the width. The double *nun* of *hisbonenus* is *bina sheb'bina*, the intermediary between *bina* and *tevuna*: go over the idea again and again, in your own words, and you absorb it and get *tevuna*.

phrases.he: וידוע גם כן שיש נו''ן כפופה ונו''ן פשוטה בבינה,
phrases.en: It's known that there is both a bent *nun* and a straight *nun*, a long *nun*, in *bina*.

phrases.he: להיות נו''ן כפופה הוא הרוחב ונו''ן פשוטה הוא האורך
phrases.en: The bent *nun* represents the width of *bina*, and the long *nun* represents the length of *bina*.
And the letter *nun* is special: when you're spelling out the name of the letter *nun*, you spell it with a long *nun*.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן בשאר מילוי האותיות
phrases.en: This is not the case with any other letter in the Hebrew *alef-beis*.

blocks.text: **It's known that there is both a bent nun and a straight nun, a long nun, in bina.** The *nun* stands for *bina*: the bent one, going out sideways, is its width; the long one, going straight down, its length.

**The letter nun is special**: its *milui* (the spelled-out name of a letter), *nun*, *vav*, *nun*, has a bent *nun* and a long one, **not the case with any other letter**. The only other doubled *milui* is *mem*, with a closed *mem*, explained later; *kaf*, *pei* and *tzadik* are not spelled with their long forms.

phrases.en: The length is included in the width.
The same thing with *tevuna*.

phrases.he: ואמנם נון הכפל בענין הנקרא התבוננות,
phrases.en: But the double *nun* that we find in the word *hisbonenus*,
like it says, "My people do not contemplate."
Which this *hisbonenus* is the inner thing of *bina*,
which is called analysis or study,
to dwell on a thing, on a matter, until you understand it clearly.

blocks.text: **The length is included in the width.** A letter's *milui* is its explanation: ask what a bent *nun* is, and the answer, *nun*, *vav*, *nun*, holds a straight *nun* too. So when you study an idea's width, with many explanations, you start to get its length: you can explain it simply too.

**The same thing with tevuna.** Its length, applying the idea outside itself, depends on its width: explaining it to yourself in many ways, with examples from outside the idea. The width of *bina* is only what is needed to understand the idea itself.

blocks.title: The motivational speaker's stories
blocks.text: Once you understand the idea, *tevuna* is like a good speaker who finds stories, examples and clever ways of putting it that are not needed to understand it but help it sink in. Motivational speakers and inspirational books mostly give stories to illustrate a point you already understand; the examples and sayings help you feel it. Any get-rich-quick tape tells you, in detail, of people its program worked for, and that gets you excited. "It's not really helping you to understand anything"; it helps you appreciate it.

**The double nun that we find in the word hisbonenus**, as in **"My people do not contemplate,"** was explained as going over it until it is clear; now we see it is a bent *nun* and a straight one. *Hisbonenus* **is the inner thing of bina, which is called analysis or study**, dwelling on a matter until it is clear.

phrases.en: This is called *bina sheb'bina*.
So this *hisbonenus* is the intermediary between *bina* and *tevuna*,
through the *nun pshuta*,

phrases.he: שמחמתו נקרא התבוננות כו' ודי למבין:

blocks.text: **This is called bina sheb'bina** (*bina* within *bina*), **the intermediary between bina and tevuna, through the nun pshuta** (the straight *nun*). The first, bent *nun* is understanding the idea, *bina* itself; going over it, the length of *bina* brings it out into *tevuna*, the straight *nun*.

So you get *tevuna* through much *hisbonenus*. If you understand the idea but cannot apply it, do the *nun* again: go over it, explain it to yourself in different ways, and you will absorb it and have *tevuna*.

The bent and straight *nun* are also two kinds of study. In *Kuntres Etz HaChaim* the Rebbe Rashab teaches learning *nigleh* (the revealed Torah), *Gemara*, by the same two steps that chapters 1 and 2 give here for *hisbonenus*: first learn it until you can say over the original's words very well, then say it in your own words. That is *tevuna*, its width described above.

Putting the idea in your own words, the width of *tevuna*, brings its length; with both comes the depth, and the *kelita*. So first you master the original, the *meshalim* in *Chassidus* or whatever it is; then you say it in your own words and apply it to different situations and your own life: "a bent *nun* learning and a straight *nun* learning."

reviewQuestions.question: What makes the light of *bina* spread out into *tevuna*, and what does the shepherd at the well show about the man of *tevuna*?
Why can a *tafsan*, or someone who knows a *pilpul* with all its *sevaros*, still be unable to rule in a particular case?
If *bina* has *middos* of its own, the intellect leaning to merit or to guilt, why is *tevuna* still needed?
What are the depth, the length and the width of *tevuna*?
Why are the emotions born from *tevuna*, the lower mother, and not from *bina*, and what does the lion in the classroom show?
How do the two *nuns* of *hisbonenus* show the way to get *tevuna*?

notes.text: Phrases he reads without translating keep their Hebrew alone: the end of line 1 (v'nikra Ima tata'a), the second half of line 11 (he explains it in the next sentences), most of line 12, the middle of line 13, the end of line 17 (kayadua), the end of line 21 (v'dai l'mevin), the clause of line 22 on the root of the letters of thought called Leah (21 w1679-1729 explains it rather than translating it), and the end of line 37. Line 33's phrase cites his explanation right after the reading (23 w1014-1048), his only rendering of it.

The atomic bomb: he says the physicists told the president to make the bomb "before the Russians make it" (22 w844-876), and that "he" (apparently Einstein) realized a bomb could be made. Historically the 1939 letter warned of Germany. Kept as he said it. Flagged (other) for a public edition, whose text drops only the clause about the Russians.

Shatik Rav (21 w877-1045): he gives it from memory ("I think it's the machlokes"), as a dispute in Beitza over an egg laid on Yom Tov and a cow born on Yom Tov. A reviewer may want to check the source; the block keeps his account.

Shechita (20 w1317-1388): he says one may slaughter with anything sharp, even slowly all day, as long as there is no pressing or ripping. Kept in the text as his illustration of the practical versus the essential; flagged (other, recommend judgment) in the November 2026 revision, since "all day" reads as a ruling and may misstate the law on a pause in the cut. The publishable text drops only that clause.

Sensitivity: two flags. The atomic-bomb mashal's "before the Russians" (22 w777-914, other), a historical slip under his name; and the shechita knife (20 w1200-1404, other, recommend judgment; see the shechita note). The contrast between how yeshiva boys and girls learn kashrus (20 w1405-1568) was flagged at first; see the review note. Left unflagged: the woman who brings her chicken to the rabbi (a stock scene; the joke is on the rabbi's pilpul), the Greeks' and America's mindsets, and motivational speakers and get-rich-quick tapes (said without contempt, as an example of tevuna's stories). The remark that it became popular to learn Gemara in the pilpul style is an opinion on a way of learning, not on people.
Kuntres Etz HaChaim (the Rebbe Rashab's tract on learning) is spelled here as a title; the table's Etz Chaim is the Arizal's book, a different work.
Review (2026-11-23): the flag on the kosher kitchen mashal (20 w1405-1568, bochurim and girls) was removed by the reviewer: printed as said.
